name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,771

entries.clue: House built quickly yards from quarry cracking (6)

indicatorNotes.from: taking Y away from QUARRY's synonym: the yards come out of it

blocks.note: cracking and fab both mean excellent

annotation.surface: A house thrown up fast, a few yards from a quarry that is cracking it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cracking' reads as a verb about stone near a quarry; it is the British adjective for excellent, as in 'a cracking day'.
annotation.definitionFit: A prefab is a prefabricated house, assembled on site from ready-made sections.

entries.clue: Sandwich crust in desk (4-3)

blocks.note: a roll is a bread roll, made into a sandwich
a crust is the top layer of something

annotation.surface: Someone has left a sandwich crust inside their desk.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a crumb in a drawer; 'in' only joins the wordplay to the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A roll-top desk has a flexible slatted cover that rolls up and down over the writing surface.

entries.clue: Comedy club jester has bottom in ladies underwear (10)

indicatorNotes.has bottom in: the jester's bottom letter, L, is put in the tights

blocks.note: FOOL, whose bottom letter L moves out
TIGHTS with the L from FOOL placed inside

annotation.surface: A comedy-club jester with his backside stuffed into women's tights.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bottom' is the last letter of FOOL in a down clue, not a backside. The Footlights is the Cambridge University student comedy club.
annotation.definitionFit: The Footlights is the famous Cambridge comedy troupe that launched many British comedians.

entries.clue: British exhibit Indian's pot (5)

blocks.note: to hang a picture is to exhibit it

annotation.surface: A British exhibition showing off an Indian's pot, as in a ceramic.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pot' looks like pottery for an exhibit; it is cannabis.
annotation.definitionFit: Bhang is an Indian preparation of cannabis, and pot is slang for cannabis.

entries.clue: As my spot could be with onset of measles? (7)

annotation.definition: As my spot could be with onset of measles?

indicatorNotes.could be: MY SPOT could be rearranged into something else

blocks.note: first letter of measles, added to the fodder

annotation.surface: Someone worrying that their spot is the start of measles.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: a spot at the onset of measles is a symptom.
annotation.definitionFit: A spot appearing as measles begins is exactly a symptom of the disease.

entries.clue: Anagram I use is ed's problem for later (4,5)

indicatorNotes.Anagram: the setter simply names the operation

annotation.surface: An editor's note: an anagram is a problem to be left for later.
annotation.walkthrough: The setter says 'Anagram' outright, which is rare; ed = editor, and the apostrophe S counts as a letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A side issue is a secondary matter, one that can be set aside for later.

entries.clue: Record is number one a short time (4)

annotation.surface: A record that sits at number one for only a short time.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Record' and 'number one' suggest the pop charts; number one means oneself, and a memo is a written record.
annotation.definitionFit: A memo is a written note kept as a record.

entries.clue: Addressing emperor with notes in order (4,3)

blocks.note: a letter addressing someone is written 'to' them

annotation.surface: Speaking to an emperor with written notes kept in order.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Notes' looks like a speaker's crib sheet; they are musical notes.
annotation.definitionFit: A tone row is a fixed ordering of the twelve chromatic notes, the basis of serial music.

entries.clue: Mother at Christmas mad to pinch one bright decoration (8,5)

indicatorNotes.to pinch: MARY pinches ILIT, holding it inside

blocks.note: Mary, the mother in the Nativity story; ILIT goes in after the M

annotation.surface: Mum at Christmas, cross, grabs a shiny bauble for the tree.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'bright decoration' looks like tinsel; the definition is just 'decoration', a medal, and 'bright' belongs to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: The Military Cross is a British gallantry medal, a decoration awarded for bravery.

entries.clue: Dome where king is regularly seen on throne (5)

indicatorNotes.regularly: at regular intervals: take every other letter of king
indicatorNotes.seen on: IG is seen sitting on the throne, placed in front of it

blocks.note: the throne is a jokey name for the toilet; loo is British for toilet

annotation.surface: A domed hall where the king sits on his throne on a regular basis.
annotation.walkthrough: The throne here is the toilet, not a royal seat.
annotation.definitionFit: An igloo is a dome-shaped Inuit shelter built of snow blocks.

entries.clue: Benefit of batting is discussed over wine (6,7)

indicatorNotes.over: in a down clue, one piece is placed above the next

blocks.note: a batting side in cricket is in
a topic that comes up is discussed

annotation.surface: The advantages of batting are debated over a glass of wine.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Benefit' reads as an advantage; it is a British state welfare payment. 'Of' sits in the wordplay as part of the phrase.
annotation.definitionFit: Income Support was a British means-tested welfare benefit.

entries.clue: Bald Omani spreading around the midriff (9)

indicatorNotes.spreading: the letters spread out into a new order

annotation.surface: A bald man from Oman getting a bit thick around the waist.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spreading' fits middle-age spread in the surface, which is why it hides well as the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: Abdominal means relating to the abdomen, the region around the midriff.

entries.clue: Bike race stage in California cleared bumpy section of road (6,4)

blocks.note: the TT is the Isle of Man motorbike race
a leg is a stage of a race
cleared = rid, as in rid of weeds

annotation.surface: A cycle-race stage in California that cleared a rough patch of road.
annotation.walkthrough: The TT (Tourist Trophy) is a motorcycle race on the Isle of Man. A cattle grid is a set of bars across a road that livestock will not cross.
annotation.definitionFit: A cattle grid is a row of metal bars across a road, jolting cars as they pass over.

entries.clue: Worry about paper clips (4)

indicatorNotes.clips: the paper clips RE, holding it inside

annotation.surface: Fussing about paper clips.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Paper clips' reads as stationery; paper is a newspaper, and clips is the containment signal.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to fret is to keep turning a worry over, gnawing at it.

entries.clue: Mystery pong bearable after muggy day (6,4)

indicatorNotes.after: BO OK comes after CLOSE D

blocks.note: BO = body odour; pong is British slang for a bad smell

annotation.surface: On a muggy day, a smell that is still just about bearable.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a sticky summer afternoon; 'Mystery' is the definition, not a description of the smell's source.
annotation.definitionFit: A closed book is something or someone impossible to understand, a mystery.

entries.clue: Englishman in Brisbane goes west to see bush (3)

indicatorNotes.goes west: in an across clue, going west means running right to left

blocks.note: pom is Australian slang for an English person

annotation.surface: An English traveller in Brisbane heads west to see the outback.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bush' suggests the Australian outback; here it is a bushy head of hair.
annotation.definitionFit: A mop is a thick untidy mass of hair, a bush of it.

entries.clue: E.g. flute maker putting lips to metal pipe (5-6)

annotation.definition: E.g. flute maker putting lips to metal pipe

blocks.note: the surface pushes an instrument maker; a flute is also a tall champagne glass
the surface pushes playing a wind instrument; the metal pipe is a blowpipe for shaping molten glass

annotation.surface: A flute maker testing an instrument by blowing into a metal pipe.
annotation.walkthrough: The flute is a champagne flute, not a musical instrument; a glassblower shapes glass by blowing down a metal blowpipe.
annotation.definitionFit: A glassblower makes vessels such as champagne flutes by blowing molten glass through a metal pipe.

entries.clue: Boxer using loaf as food (9)

annotation.definitionNote: ALIMENTAL is an adjective, 'relating to food'; 'as food' is the adjectival phrase it replaces

blocks.note: loaf = head (rhyming slang: loaf of bread); using your head is mental work

annotation.surface: A boxer eating a loaf of bread as his food.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Loaf' sits naturally beside food in the surface; it is Cockney rhyming slang for head, so 'using loaf' is mental effort.
annotation.definitionFit: Alimental means relating to food or nourishment.

entries.clue: Aren't ropes aboard ship in irreproachable condition? (11)

indicatorNotes.aboard: the words go on board the ship, inside SS

blocks.note: lines are ropes, especially on a ship

annotation.surface: A sailor asking whether the ship's rigging is in perfect order.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the surface asks about shipshape ropes while the answer is a moral quality.
annotation.definitionFit: Saintliness is the condition of being saintly, beyond reproach.

entries.clue: Progressing while it's wet on Pen-y-ghent? (2,5)

blocks.note: an idiom for under way, like a plan that has been set going
Pen-y-ghent is a Yorkshire hill, where local speech clips 'the' to t'; the question mark flags the dialect

annotation.surface: Hikers pressing on up a Yorkshire hill in wet weather.
annotation.walkthrough: Pen-y-ghent is a hill in the Yorkshire Dales, and Yorkshire speakers shorten 'the' to t', so 'in the rain' there is 'in t' rain'.
annotation.definitionFit: Something in train is under way, progressing.

entries.clue: American's mate runs out of brandy (3)

indicatorNotes.out of: R is taken out of the brandy

blocks.note: marc is a brandy distilled from grape skins
r = runs in cricket scoring; removed

annotation.surface: A US buddy runs out of brandy at the bar.
annotation.walkthrough: Mac is an American way of addressing a man, like 'buddy' or 'pal'.
annotation.definitionFit: Americans call a man they are addressing 'Mac', much as the British say 'mate'.

entries.clue: Country market's opening with out of date eggs (7)

blocks.note: ova = eggs, in Latin and biology

annotation.surface: A rural market opening with a tray of stale eggs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Country market' reads as one phrase, a farmers' market; 'Country' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Moldova is one country among many, the small state between Romania and Ukraine.

entries.clue: Animals walk around (4)

indicatorNotes.around: to turn around is to face the other way, so STEP faces the other way and reads right to left

annotation.surface: Animals strolling about.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Walk' looks like a verb the animals are doing; it supplies STEP, turned round.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: pets are the animals people keep at home for company.

entries.clue: Failing roll, I'd accept sandwiches brought over (10)

indicatorNotes.sandwiches: the words hold the answer inside them

blocks.note: rOLL I'D ACCEPt, read right to left

annotation.surface: Someone refusing a bread roll, but agreeing to take the sandwiches that are passed across.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Roll' and 'sandwiches' make a lunch scene, so 'sandwiches' reads as food rather than the signal that the answer lies inside.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: peccadillo, Spanish for 'little sin', names a minor failing of character.

entries.clue: Archer in court with police outside (5)

indicatorNotes.outside: the police stand outside, round UP, the way officers flank a defendant in the dock

blocks.note: CID = Criminal Investigation Department, British police detectives
to be up before a judge is to be in court

annotation.surface: An archer standing trial with police officers flanking him.
annotation.walkthrough: The archer is Cupid with his bow and arrows, not a sportsman on a charge.
annotation.definitionFit: Cupid, the Roman god of love, is pictured as an archer firing arrows.

entries.clue: Nigerian playing bingo has crossed out number (4)

indicatorNotes.playing: the letters are played around with
indicatorNotes.has crossed out: a letter is struck out of the word

annotation.surface: A Nigerian at a bingo game has crossed out a number on the card.
annotation.walkthrough: Crossing out numbers is exactly what bingo players do, so the deletion signal is well disguised.
annotation.definitionFit: The Igbo are a people of south-eastern Nigeria, so an Igbo is a Nigerian.

entries.clue: Pigeon confused with rat? One flutters (6-3)

indicatorNotes.confused: confused means jumbled, and jumbled letters no longer stand in their original order

annotation.surface: A pigeon being mistaken for a rat as it flaps about.
annotation.walkthrough: The flutterer seems to be the pigeon; the answer is a butterfly.
annotation.definitionFit: The orange-tip is a white butterfly whose males have orange wing tips.

entries.clue: Tramps less hot in some wind (5)

indicatorNotes.less: 'less' means lacking, as in 'the price less tax', so the tramps lose their H

blocks.note: h = hot, as on taps; removed

annotation.surface: Tramps feeling less warm out in the wind.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wind' suggests weather; here it is wind instruments.
annotation.definitionFit: Oboes are woodwind instruments, part of an orchestra's wind section.

entries.clue: Thin sheet up to storing data (7)

indicatorNotes.storing: a store holds goods inside it, so TIL holds INFO

annotation.surface: A thin sheet for storing data, like a memory film.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Thin sheet' is plain foil; the wordplay is til around info.
annotation.definitionFit: Tinfoil is metal rolled into a very thin sheet.

entries.clue: Child put back Tango in response to strict order (6)

indicatorNotes.put back: to put something back is to send it the way it came, so KID runs backwards

blocks.note: Tango = T in the NATO alphabet
at = in response to, as in 'at his command'

annotation.surface: A child reluctantly doing the tango because a strict order told them to.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In response to' looks like a link into the definition, but it supplies AT, as in 'at her request'.
annotation.definitionFit: A diktat is an order imposed without discussion.
